modules.title: Object Oriented Programming 1
modules.overview: This module introduces fundamental concepts of object-oriented programming including classes, objects, inheritance, and polymorphism.
modules.prerequisitesText: - Basic programming knowledge (typically from an introductory programming module)
outcomes: Understand and implement core object-oriented concepts
Design and implement classes and objects
Apply principles of inheritance and polymorphism
Develop simple object-oriented programs
assessment: Coursework: Programming assignments
Exam: Final examination covering theoretical and practical aspects

modules.title: Object Oriented Programming 2
modules.overview: This module builds upon the foundational concepts introduced in Object Oriented Programming 1, exploring advanced object-oriented programming techniques including design patterns, exception handling, generic programming, and advanced use of inheritance and polymorphism. Students will develop larger-scale object-oriented applications with emphasis on code quality, testing, and maintainability.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1811 Object Oriented Programming 1]]
- Basic understanding of classes, objects, inheritance, and polymorphism
- [[CS1821 Programming Laboratory]] (concurrent or completed)
outcomes: Apply advanced object-oriented programming concepts including templates/generics and operator overloading
Implement and utilise common design patterns (Singleton, Factory, Observer, Strategy)
Develop robust code with proper exception handling and resource management
Design and implement programs using UML class diagrams
Write unit tests and apply test-driven development principles
Analyse and refactor existing code to improve design quality
assessment: Coursework: Programming assignments (individual and pair-based)
Project: Larger-scale object-oriented application development
Exam: Written examination covering design patterns and advanced OO concepts

modules.title: Software Development
modules.overview: This 2025-2026 module provides an alternative first-year software development route for students with prior programming experience, developing practical programming, design, testing, and implementation skills for later software engineering modules.
modules.prerequisitesText: - Prior programming experience or permission to take the Software Development route
outcomes: Design and implement software using appropriate programming constructs
Apply basic software development, testing, and debugging practices
Use development tools to build maintainable programs
Prepare for intermediate software engineering modules
assessment: Coursework and practical programming assessment
Examination or timed programming assessment

modules.title: Programming Laboratory
modules.overview: This practical, project-based module provides students with hands-on programming experience alongside the core theory modules. Students work on structured programming exercises and small projects that reinforce concepts from concurrent modules. The lab setting emphasises good programming practices, debugging techniques, version control, and collaborative development.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- Introductory programming experience
- Concurrent enrolment with [[CS1811 Object Oriented Programming 1]] or equivalent
outcomes: Develop, test, and debug programs in a structured laboratory environment
Use version control systems (e.g., Git) for source code management
Apply systematic debugging and testing strategies
Work effectively on programming tasks within time constraints
Document code appropriately using comments and documentation tools
Navigate the development toolchain (compiler, linker, build systems, IDE)
assessment: Continuous assessment: Lab exercises and programming assignments
Practical tests: Timed programming assessments
Project work: Small to medium programming projects

modules.title: Programming Laboratory
modules.overview: This intensive practical module provides hands-on programming experience across multiple domains. Students work on substantial programming projects including robot programming, developing software engineering skills through group work, and building competence in essential programming tools and practices. The module emphasises practical application of programming concepts through project-based learning.
modules.prerequisitesText: - None (core first-year module)
outcomes: Design, implement, test and debug substantial programs
Work effectively in a team on a software development project
Apply version control and collaborative development practices
Program robotics platforms and embedded systems
Demonstrate proficiency in multiple programming paradigms
Read and understand technical documentation and specifications
assessment: Practical programming assignments
Robot programming project (group work)
Continuous assessment through laboratory exercises
Written examination

modules.title: Internet Services
modules.overview: This module introduces the fundamental technologies and protocols that underpin the internet and web services. Topics include network architectures, the TCP/IP protocol stack, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS, email protocols, and basic web server configuration. Students gain both theoretical understanding and practical experience in configuring and interacting with core internet services.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- Basic understanding of computer systems ([[CS1870 Machine Fundamentals]] or equivalent)
- Familiarity with operating a computer and basic networking concepts
outcomes: Explain the architecture and operation of the TCP/IP protocol suite
Configure and manage basic internet services (web servers, DNS, email)
Understand the client-server model and its application to internet services
Analyse HTTP traffic and understand web service communication
Implement simple network clients and servers
Describe the security considerations relevant to internet services
assessment: Coursework: Practical exercises in configuring internet services
Laboratory reports: Documentation of network experiments
Exam: Written examination covering protocols and architectures

modules.title: Mathematical Structures
modules.overview: This module provides the mathematical foundations necessary for computer science. Topics include propositional and predicate logic, set theory, relations and functions, proof techniques (induction, contradiction), combinatorics, graph theory, and an introduction to algebraic structures. The module emphasises rigorous mathematical reasoning and its application to computing problems.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- A-level Mathematics (or equivalent)
- No specific programming prerequisites
outcomes: Apply propositional and predicate logic to model and reason about computational problems
Use set theory, relations, and functions as formal modelling tools
Construct rigorous mathematical proofs using appropriate techniques
Solve combinatorial problems and apply counting principles
Analyse graph structures and apply graph algorithms
Recognise and apply algebraic structures relevant to computing
assessment: Coursework: Problem sheets and assignments
Mid-term test: Progress assessment
Exam: Final written examination

modules.title: Machine Fundamentals
modules.overview: This module introduces the fundamental concepts of computer hardware and low-level programming. Topics include digital logic, binary representation, processor architecture, memory hierarchy, assembly language programming, and the interface between hardware and software. Students gain an understanding of how high-level programs execute on physical machines.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- Basic mathematics (binary, hexadecimal arithmetic)
- No prior programming experience required
outcomes: Explain the representation of data at the machine level (binary, hexadecimal, two's complement, floating point)
Describe the basic organisation of a processor (ALU, control unit, registers, memory)
Write and debug simple assembly language programs
Understand the fetch-decode-execute cycle and instruction pipelining
Explain memory hierarchy and its impact on performance
Describe how high-level language constructs are translated to machine code
assessment: Coursework: Assembly programming assignments
Laboratory work: Digital logic simulations and hardware exercises
Exam: Written examination covering architecture and low-level concepts

modules.title: Software Design
modules.overview: This module introduces the principles and practices of software design. Topics include the software development lifecycle, requirements analysis, system modelling using UML, architectural design, user interface design principles, and design documentation. The module emphasises a systematic approach to designing software systems before implementation.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1811 Object Oriented Programming 1]] (concurrent or completed)
- Basic programming competency
outcomes: Apply a systematic software design process to solve problems
Create and interpret UML diagrams (class, sequence, activity, state machine)
Analyse and document software requirements
Evaluate alternative design solutions using appropriate criteria
Design user interfaces following established principles
Prepare design documentation suitable for use in development teams
assessment: Coursework: Design exercises and UML modelling tasks
Project: Complete software design document for a given problem
Exam: Written examination covering design principles and methodologies

modules.title: Software Engineering
modules.overview: This module provides a comprehensive introduction to software engineering principles and practices. Topics include software process models (Waterfall, Agile, Scrum), requirements engineering, software architecture, design patterns, testing strategies, software maintenance, and project management fundamentals. Students apply these concepts through team-based software development projects.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1890 Software Design]]
- [[CS1812 Object Oriented Programming 2]]
- [[CS1821 Programming Laboratory]]
- Proficiency in at least one programming language
outcomes: Select and apply appropriate software development process models
Elicit, analyse, document, and validate software requirements
Design software architectures using appropriate styles and patterns
Implement and execute a comprehensive testing strategy (unit, integration, system)
Apply refactoring and software maintenance techniques
Estimate project effort and manage software development schedules
Work effectively as part of a software development team
assessment: Coursework: Team-based software development project with deliverables
Group report: Documentation of process, design decisions, and reflections
Individual contribution assessment
Exam: Written examination covering software engineering theory

modules.title: Team Project
modules.overview: This major module requires students to work in teams to develop a substantial software project from inception to delivery. Teams of 4-6 students collaboratively design, implement, test, and deliver a software system, applying the principles of software engineering, project management, and team collaboration. The module simulates real-world software development and emphasises both technical and interpersonal skills.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS2800 Software Engineering]]
- [[CS1812 Object Oriented Programming 2]]
- [[CS1890 Software Design]]
- Proficiency in programming and development tools
outcomes: Plan, manage, and execute a substantial team-based software project
Apply software engineering methodologies to a realistic development scenario
Design and implement a software solution that meets specified requirements
Use professional development tools (version control, issue tracking, CI/CD)
Communicate technical work effectively through reports, presentations, and demonstrations
Reflect critically on team processes and individual contribution
Resolve conflicts and coordinate work across team members
assessment: Project deliverables: Software product with source code and documentation
Team reports: Requirements, design, testing, and project management documentation
Presentations: Project proposal, progress review, and final demonstration
Peer assessment: Evaluation of individual contributions within the team
Individual report: Personal reflection on the project experience

modules.title: Small Enterprise Team Project
modules.overview: This module extends the team project experience by focusing on the unique challenges of developing software for small enterprises and startups. Students work with real or simulated clients in a small business context, addressing constraints such as limited resources, rapid iteration, and close client collaboration. The module emphasises agile practices, MVP development, and entrepreneurial thinking.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS2800 Software Engineering]]
- [[CS1812 Object Oriented Programming 2]]
- [[CS2810 Team Project]] (concurrent or completed)
- Programming competency and team-working experience
outcomes: Adapt software engineering practices to the small enterprise context
Elicit and prioritise requirements in collaboration with real or simulated clients
Develop and iterate a minimum viable product (MVP) under resource constraints
Apply lean and agile methodologies in a fast-paced environment
Demonstrate entrepreneurial awareness in software development decisions
Communicate effectively with non-technical stakeholders
assessment: Project deliverables: Working software product with documentation
Client engagement: Requirement sessions, progress reviews, final presentation
Team reports: Process documentation and retrospective
Peer and client assessment of team and individual contributions

modules.title: Internet Services
modules.overview: This advanced module explores the design, implementation, and deployment of internet-based services. Building on foundational networking concepts, topics include RESTful API design, web services (SOAP, REST, GraphQL), cloud computing fundamentals, service-oriented architecture, containerisation (Docker), microservices, and performance considerations for internet-scale services.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1840 Internet Services]] or equivalent networking knowledge
- [[CS1812 Object Oriented Programming 2]]
- Proficiency in at least one programming language for server-side development
outcomes: Design and implement RESTful and GraphQL web services
Deploy and manage internet services using cloud platforms
Apply containerisation (Docker) and orchestration concepts
Understand and evaluate service-oriented and microservice architectures
Implement security measures for internet services (authentication, authorisation, HTTPS)
Measure and optimise the performance of internet services
Use API documentation standards (OpenAPI/Swagger)
assessment: Coursework: Implementation of internet services with API endpoints
Practical exercises: Containerisation, deployment, and performance testing
Project: Design and deploy a complete internet service
Exam: Written examination covering service architecture and protocols

modules.title: Operating Systems
modules.overview: This module provides a comprehensive study of operating system concepts and design. Topics include process and thread management, CPU scheduling, memory management (paging, segmentation, virtual memory), file systems, I/O management, deadlock detection and prevention, and an introduction to distributed systems. The module includes practical exercises in systems programming.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1870 Machine Fundamentals]]
- [[CS1811 Object Oriented Programming 1]]
- Understanding of data structures and programming in C/C++
outcomes: Explain the roles and responsibilities of an operating system
Implement process management and scheduling algorithms
Analyse memory management techniques and virtual memory systems
Describe file system organisation and implementation
Identify, prevent, and handle deadlock situations
Write systems-level programs that interact with the OS (system calls, signals)
Understand the principles of concurrency and synchronisation
assessment: Coursework: Systems programming assignments (process management, memory, file systems)
Practical exercises: Simulating OS algorithms
Exam: Written examination covering OS theory and design

modules.title: Databases
modules.overview: This module introduces the theory and practice of database systems. Topics include the relational model, SQL (DDL, DML, DQL), database design using entity-relationship modelling, normalisation, transaction processing, concurrency control, indexing and query optimisation, and an introduction to NoSQL databases. Students gain practical experience in designing, querying, and managing databases.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]] (useful for relational algebra)
- Programming experience sufficient to implement database-connected applications
outcomes: Design relational databases using entity-relationship modelling and normalisation
Write complex SQL queries including joins, subqueries, aggregation, and transactions
Implement database applications using a programming language (e.g., Python, Java)
Understand transaction processing and concurrency control mechanisms
Explain indexing strategies and query optimisation techniques
Compare relational and NoSQL database approaches for different use cases
Apply database security principles (access control, SQL injection prevention)
assessment: Coursework: Database design exercises and SQL assignments
Practical project: Design and implement a database for a given application
Exam: Written examination covering database theory and design

modules.title: Algorithms and Complexity
modules.overview: This module covers the design and analysis of algorithms, focusing on algorithm efficiency and computational complexity. Topics include asymptotic analysis (Big-O notation), sorting and searching algorithms, divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, graph algorithms, and an introduction to NP-completeness. Emphasis is placed on rigorous analysis of time and space complexity.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]]
- [[CS1811 Object Oriented Programming 1]]
- Proficiency in at least one programming language for implementing algorithms
outcomes: Analyse algorithm efficiency using asymptotic notation (Big-O, Theta, Omega)
Design and implement efficient algorithms using divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, and greedy approaches
Implement and analyse fundamental graph algorithms (BFS, DFS, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees)
Apply algorithmic problem-solving strategies to new problems
Classify problems by complexity class (P, NP, NP-complete)
Understand the trade-offs between time and space complexity
Implement correct and efficient data structures (heaps, hash tables, balanced trees)
assessment: Coursework: Algorithm implementation and analysis assignments
Problem sheets: Written exercises in algorithm design and complexity analysis
Exam: Final written examination covering algorithm analysis and design

modules.title: Multi-dimensional Data Processing
modules.overview: This module covers techniques for processing, analysing, and visualising multi-dimensional datasets. Topics include data representation in multiple dimensions, dimensionality reduction (PCA, t-SNE), multi-dimensional indexing and search structures (R-trees, kd-trees), similarity measures, clustering algorithms, and visualisation techniques for high-dimensional data. Applications include scientific computing, data analytics, and information retrieval.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]] (recommended background)
- [[CS2860 Algorithms and Complexity]] (recommended background)
- Programming proficiency (Python recommended)
- Basic statistics and linear algebra knowledge
outcomes: Represent and manipulate multi-dimensional data using appropriate data structures
Apply dimensionality reduction techniques to high-dimensional datasets
Implement efficient multi-dimensional search and indexing algorithms
Apply clustering algorithms to discover patterns in data
Design effective visualisations for multi-dimensional data
Evaluate the quality of dimensionality reduction and clustering results
Process large-scale multi-dimensional data efficiently
assessment: Coursework: Programming assignments implementing multi-dimensional algorithms
Project: Data analysis and visualisation of a real-world multi-dimensional dataset
Exam: Written examination covering theory and techniques

modules.title: Symbolic Artificial Intelligence
modules.overview: This module introduces the classical, symbolic approach to artificial intelligence. Topics include knowledge representation (logic, semantic networks, frames, ontologies), search algorithms (uninformed, informed, heuristic, adversarial), automated reasoning and inference, planning, rule-based expert systems, and an introduction to natural language processing from a symbolic perspective.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]] (particularly logic)
- [[CS2860 Algorithms and Complexity]]
- Programming proficiency
outcomes: Represent knowledge using logical formalisms (propositional logic, first-order logic)
Implement and analyse search algorithms for problem-solving
Design and implement rule-based reasoning systems
Apply automated planning techniques to structured problems
Evaluate the strengths and limitations of symbolic AI approaches
Understand the historical context and philosophical questions of AI
Compare symbolic AI with connectionist (neural) approaches
assessment: Coursework: Implementation of search algorithms and reasoning systems
Problem sheets: Knowledge representation and logical inference exercises
Project: Build a rule-based expert system or planning system
Exam: Written examination covering AI theory and techniques

modules.title: Introduction to Information Security
modules.overview: This module provides a broad introduction to information security. Topics include security fundamentals (confidentiality, integrity, availability), cryptographic primitives, security policies, authentication and access control, network security basics, web security, malware, social engineering, and legal/ethical aspects of cyber security. The module establishes the foundational knowledge required for advanced security modules.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1870 Machine Fundamentals]] (recommended)
- [[CS1840 Internet Services]] (recommended)
- Basic understanding of computer networks and operating systems
outcomes: Explain the core principles of information security (CIA triad)
Understand and apply basic cryptographic concepts (symmetric/asymmetric encryption, hashing)
Identify common security threats and vulnerabilities
Implement basic authentication and access control mechanisms
Recognise common attack patterns (phishing, SQL injection, XSS, buffer overflows)
Understand the legal and ethical framework for information security
Apply security best practices to protect systems and data
assessment: Coursework: Security analysis exercises and reports
Practical assignments: Security tool usage and basic penetration testing
Exam: Written examination covering security fundamentals

modules.title: Computer and Network Security
modules.overview: This module provides an in-depth study of computer and network security. Topics include network security protocols (IPSec, TLS/SSL, SSH), firewalls and intrusion detection/prevention systems, VPNs, wireless security, authentication protocols, access control models, operating system security, and security evaluation and assurance. The module combines theoretical understanding with practical configuration and analysis.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[IY2760 Introduction to Information Security]]
- [[CS1840 Internet Services]] or equivalent networking knowledge
- [[CS2850 Operating Systems]] (recommended)
outcomes: Analyse and configure network security protocols (IPSec, TLS, SSH)
Design and implement firewall rules and network segmentation
Configure and evaluate intrusion detection/prevention systems
Implement secure VPN solutions
Analyse and evaluate authentication protocols
Apply operating system security mechanisms
Conduct security assessments of networked systems
Understand security evaluation standards and methodologies
assessment: Coursework: Network security configuration exercises
Practical assignments: Firewall rules, IDS configuration, security assessments
Project: Security audit of a networked system
Exam: Written examination covering network and computer security

modules.title: IT Project Management
modules.overview: This module covers the principles and practices of managing IT projects. Topics include project lifecycle models, project planning and scheduling, risk management, resource estimation, budget management, quality assurance, stakeholder management, and agile project management frameworks (Scrum, Kanban). The module prepares students for leadership roles in software development and IT delivery.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS2800 Software Engineering]] or equivalent experience
- Some team project experience ( [[CS2810 Team Project]]
outcomes: Develop comprehensive project plans including schedules, budgets, and resource allocations
Identify, assess, and mitigate IT project risks
Apply appropriate project management methodologies (Waterfall, Agile, Hybrid)
Monitor and control project progress using appropriate metrics
Manage stakeholder expectations and communicate project status effectively
Lead project teams and resolve conflicts
Understand professional, legal, and ethical issues in IT project management
assessment: Coursework: Project management plans and risk assessments
Case study analysis: Evaluation of real-world IT project successes and failures
Group exercise: Simulated project management scenarios
Exam: Written examination covering PM theory and frameworks

modules.title: Software Verification
modules.overview: This module covers formal and informal techniques for verifying the correctness of software systems. Topics include formal specification languages, program verification using Hoare logic, model checking, static analysis, theorem proving, and software testing methodologies. The module emphasises rigorous approaches to ensuring software reliability and safety.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]] (logic and proof techniques)
- [[CS2800 Software Engineering]]
- [[CS2860 Algorithms and Complexity]]
- Proficiency in at least one programming language
outcomes: Write formal specifications for software components
Apply Hoare logic to prove program correctness
Use model checking tools to verify system properties
Implement and apply static analysis techniques
Design systematic testing strategies based on formal criteria
Understand the theoretical foundations of program verification
Evaluate the limitations and trade-offs of different verification approaches
assessment: Coursework: Formal specification and verification exercises
Practical assignments: Using verification tools (model checkers, static analysers)
Project: Formal verification of a non-trivial program
Exam: Written examination covering verification theory

modules.title: Compilers and Code Generation
modules.overview: This module covers the theory and practice of compiler construction. Topics include lexical analysis, syntax analysis (parsing), semantic analysis, intermediate representations, code optimisation, and code generation. Students implement key components of a compiler, gaining a deep understanding of how high-level programs are translated into executable code.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1870 Machine Fundamentals]]
- [[CS2860 Algorithms and Complexity]]
- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]]
- Proficiency in a systems programming language (C, C++, Rust)
- [[CS3480 Software Language Engineering]] (concurrent or completed, recommended)
outcomes: Design and implement lexical analysers (scanners) using regular expressions
Implement parsers using context-free grammars (recursive descent, LALR, LL)
Construct abstract syntax trees and perform semantic analysis
Generate intermediate code from abstract syntax trees
Apply code optimisation techniques (constant folding, loop optimisation, register allocation)
Generate target machine code or bytecode
Understand the trade-offs in compiler design decisions
assessment: Coursework: Incremental implementation of compiler components
Project: Complete compiler for a small programming language
Exam: Written examination covering compiler theory and algorithms

modules.title: Software Language Engineering
modules.overview: This module covers the design, implementation, and analysis of programming and domain-specific languages. Topics include language design principles, syntax and semantics, type systems, domain-specific languages (DSLs), language workbenches, metaprogramming, and the theoretical foundations of programming languages (lambda calculus, type theory).
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]] (logic and algebra)
- [[CS1812 Object Oriented Programming 2]]
- [[CS2860 Algorithms and Complexity]]
outcomes: Analyse and compare programming language paradigms and their features
Design and implement domain-specific languages (DSLs)
Understand type systems and their role in program correctness
Apply formal semantics (operational, denotational, axiomatic) to describe language behaviour
Implement interpreters and compilers for small languages
Use language workbenches to develop DSLs
Understand metaprogramming and code generation techniques
assessment: Coursework: Language design and implementation exercises
Project: Design and implement a domain-specific language
Exam: Written examination covering language theory and design

modules.title: Computational Optimization
modules.overview: This module covers the theory and practice of computational optimisation techniques. Topics include linear programming, integer programming, convex optimisation, gradient-based methods, metaheuristic algorithms (genetic algorithms, simulated annealing), constraint satisfaction, and multi-objective optimisation. Applications include resource allocation, scheduling, logistics, and engineering design.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]]
- [[CS2860 Algorithms and Complexity]]
- Linear algebra and basic calculus
- Programming proficiency (Python recommended)
outcomes: Formulate real-world problems as mathematical optimisation problems
Solve linear and integer programming problems using appropriate algorithms
Apply convex optimisation techniques to appropriate problems
Implement and apply gradient descent and its variants
Design and apply metaheuristic algorithms for hard problems
Use constraint programming for combinatorial problems
Compare and select appropriate optimisation techniques for different problem classes
assessment: Coursework: Implementation of optimisation algorithms
Problem sheets: Mathematical formulation and analysis
Project: Apply optimisation techniques to a real-world problem
Exam: Written examination covering optimisation theory

modules.title: Functional Programming and Applications
modules.overview: This 2025-2026 module introduces functional programming principles and applications, including recursion, abstraction, higher-order functions, data types, pattern matching, and combining functional and object-oriented programming styles.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1811 Object Oriented Programming 1]] or equivalent programming experience
- [[CS1812 Object Oriented Programming 2]] or [[CS1813 Software Development]] recommended
outcomes: Explain the foundations and advantages of functional programming
Use recursion, abstraction, higher-order functions, and functional data types
Apply pattern matching and functional design techniques
Compare functional, imperative, and object-oriented programming paradigms
Develop applications using functional programming concepts
assessment: Coursework
Examination

modules.title: Quantum Computation
modules.overview: This module provides an introduction to the theory and practice of quantum computing. Topics include the mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics (state vectors, superposition, measurement), quantum gates and circuits, quantum algorithms (Deutsch-Jozsa, Shor's algorithm, Grover's search), quantum error correction, and the physics of quantum computation. The module covers both theoretical principles and practical implementation using quantum computing frameworks.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]]
- [[CS2860 Algorithms and Complexity]]
- Linear algebra (vector spaces, complex numbers, matrix operations)
- Physics background desirable but not essential
outcomes: Explain the fundamental principles of quantum computing (superposition, entanglement, interference)
Represent quantum states mathematically and apply quantum gates
Design and analyse simple quantum circuits
Understand and explain key quantum algorithms (Deutsch-Jozsa, Shor, Grover)
Compare quantum and classical computational complexity
Implement quantum algorithms using quantum computing frameworks
Understand the current limitations and challenges in quantum computing
assessment: Coursework: Quantum circuit design and algorithm implementation
Problem sheets: Mathematical exercises in quantum mechanics and computation
Project: Implement and analyse a quantum algorithm
Exam: Written examination covering quantum computing theory

modules.title: Full Unit Project
modules.overview: This module is the mandatory final-year individual project for BSc Computer Science students at Royal Holloway. Students undertake a substantial piece of independent work under the supervision of a member of academic staff, demonstrating their ability to plan, execute, and deliver a significant software or research project. The project runs across the full academic year, requiring students to apply and integrate knowledge from across their degree programme. **Official data:** 10 contact hours, 290 self-study hours, 100% coursework assessment, 30 credits, FHEQ Level 6, Mandatory Condonable (MC). > The BCS and EQANIE accreditation requirements mandate that students must successfully complete and pass the final year project.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- Successful completion of all Year 1 and Year 2 compulsory modules
- [[CS2810 Team Project]] or [[CS2815 Small enterprise team project]] provides relevant team-based project experience
- Relevant pathway modules providing domain knowledge for project topic
outcomes: Plan and manage a substantial independent project from inception to completion
Research and evaluate relevant literature, technologies, and methodologies
Design, implement, and test a significant software system or conduct rigorous research
Critically evaluate their own work and reflect on the process and outcomes
Communicate technical work effectively through written reports and oral presentations
Demonstrate professional judgement, ethical awareness, and independent problem-solving
assessment: **Project Proposal & Ethics Clearance** (formative)
**Interim Report / Progress Review** (typically 20-30%)
**Final Dissertation / Report** (typically 50-60%)
**Demonstration & Oral Presentation / Viva** (typically 20-30%)

modules.title: Advanced Algorithms and Complexity
modules.overview: This module explores advanced topics in algorithm design and computational complexity theory. Topics include advanced data structures (Fibonacci heaps, splay trees, union-find), amortised analysis, approximation algorithms, randomised algorithms, online algorithms, parameterised complexity, and advanced NP-completeness reductions. The module provides a rigorous treatment of the theoretical foundations of efficient computation.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS2860 Algorithms and Complexity]] (strong performance expected)
- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]]
- Comfortable with mathematical proof techniques and asymptotic analysis
outcomes: Design and analyse algorithms using advanced techniques (amortised analysis, potential functions)
Implement and analyse advanced data structures
Design approximation algorithms for NP-hard problems
Analyse randomised algorithms using probabilistic methods
Apply parameterised complexity concepts to classify problems
Construct NP-completeness reductions for complex problems
Understand the limits of efficient computation
assessment: Coursework: Algorithm design and analysis problem sets
Programming assignments: Implementation of advanced algorithms
Exam: Rigorous written examination covering advanced theoretical content

modules.title: Machine Learning
modules.overview: This module provides a broad introduction to machine learning. Topics include supervised learning (linear regression, logistic regression, decision trees, support vector machines, neural networks), unsupervised learning (k-means, hierarchical clustering, Gaussian mixture models), model evaluation and selection (cross-validation, bias-variance trade-off, regularisation), and an introduction to deep learning. The module emphasises both theoretical understanding and practical application.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]] (probability, linear algebra)
- [[CS2860 Algorithms and Complexity]]
- [[CS2900 Multi-dimensional Data Processing]] (recommended)
- Programming proficiency in Python
- Basic statistics knowledge
outcomes: Understand and implement core supervised learning algorithms
Apply unsupervised learning techniques for pattern discovery
Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics and validation strategies
Apply regularisation techniques to prevent overfitting
Preprocess and transform data for machine learning pipelines
Use machine learning libraries effectively (scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch)
Communicate results and model limitations effectively
assessment: Coursework: Implementation of ML algorithms from scratch
Practical assignments: Applied ML using established libraries
Project: End-to-end machine learning project on a real dataset
Exam: Written examination covering ML theory and methodology

modules.title: Computational Finance
modules.overview: This module applies computational techniques to problems in finance. Topics include financial data analysis, time series modelling, algorithmic trading strategies, portfolio optimisation, risk management, derivatives pricing (Monte Carlo methods, binomial trees), and machine learning applications in finance. The module combines programming, statistical analysis, and financial theory.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS3920 Machine Learning]] (recommended)
- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]] (probability and statistics)
- Programming proficiency (Python)
- Basic understanding of financial markets and instruments (desirable but not essential)
outcomes: Analyse financial time series data using statistical methods
Implement algorithmic trading strategies and backtest their performance
Apply portfolio optimisation techniques (Markowitz, Black-Litterman)
Price financial derivatives using Monte Carlo simulation and lattice methods
Apply machine learning techniques to financial prediction tasks
Assess and manage financial risk using computational tools
Understand the limitations and risks of quantitative finance models
assessment: Coursework: Programming assignments implementing financial models
Project: Develop and backtest a trading strategy or risk management system
Exam: Written examination covering computational finance theory and methods

modules.title: Intelligent Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
modules.overview: This module covers the design and implementation of intelligent agents and multi-agent systems. Topics include agent architectures (reactive, deliberative, hybrid), agent communication languages, coordination and cooperation mechanisms, negotiation protocols, distributed problem solving, and applications in robotics, simulation, and decentralised systems.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[CS2910 Symbolic Artificial Intelligence]]
- [[CS2860 Algorithms and Complexity]]
- Programming proficiency
- [[CS3920 Machine Learning]] (recommended)
outcomes: Design and implement intelligent agents using appropriate architectures
Implement agent communication and interaction protocols

modules.title: Deep Learning
modules.overview: This module provides a comprehensive introduction to deep learning. Topics include neural network architectures (feedforward, convolutional, recurrent, transformers), training techniques (backpropagation, optimisation, regularisation, batch normalisation), representation learning, generative models (GANs, VAEs, diffusion models), and practical considerations for deploying deep learning models. The module emphasises both theoretical foundations and hands-on implementation.

modules.title: Natural Language Processing
modules.overview: This module introduces the theory and practice of natural language processing. Topics include text preprocessing, language modelling (n-grams, neural language models), part-of-speech tagging, parsing (constituency, dependency), named entity recognition, sentiment analysis, machine translation, and modern transformer-based models (BERT, GPT, T5). The module covers both traditional statistical NLP and contemporary deep learning approaches.
modules.prerequisitesText:

- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]] (probability, statistics)

modules.title: Security Management
modules.overview: This module covers the management of information security in organisations. Topics include security governance frameworks (ISO 27001, NIST, COBIT), security policy development, risk assessment and management methodologies, business continuity planning, incident response management, security awareness and training, compliance and audit, and security metrics. The module emphasises the organisational and human dimensions of security.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[IY2760 Introduction to Information Security]]
- Understanding of organisational structures and management principles
- [[CS3003 IT Project Management]] (recommended)

modules.title: Smart Cards, RFIDs and Embedded Systems Security
modules.overview: This module covers security challenges and solutions for smart cards, RFID systems, and embedded devices. Topics include smart card architectures and operating systems, cryptographic coprocessors, RFID communication protocols, near-field communication (NFC), embedded system security (secure boot, trusted execution environments), side-channel attacks, fault injection, and security for IoT devices.

- [[IY2760 Introduction to Information Security]]
- [[CS1870 Machine Fundamentals]] (hardware knowledge)
- Basic cryptography understanding ([[IY3660 Applications of Cryptography]] recommended)
- Embedded systems or electronics knowledge (desirable)

Implement security mechanisms for embedded systems

modules.title: Digital Forensics
modules.overview: This module covers the principles and practices of digital forensics investigation. Topics include forensic methodology, evidence acquisition and preservation, disk and file system forensics, memory forensics, network forensics, mobile device forensics, forensic analysis tools, anti-forensics techniques, and legal considerations for digital evidence. The module emphasises both technical skills and adherence to legal and ethical standards.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[IY2760 Introduction to Information Security]]
- [[CS2850 Operating Systems]] (file systems, memory management)
- [[CS1840 Internet Services]] (network fundamentals)
- Understanding of legal frameworks for evidence (desirable)

Practical assignments: Hands-on forensic analysis exercises

Exam: Written examination covering forensics methodology and techniques

modules.title: Critical Infrastructure Security
modules.overview: This module addresses the security of critical national infrastructure systems. Topics include industrial control systems (ICS) and SCADA architecture, cyber-physical system security, threat landscapes for critical infrastructure, security standards for critical infrastructure (NERC CIP, IEC 62443), risk assessment for safety-critical systems, incident response for industrial environments, and national/international policy frameworks for infrastructure protection.
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[IY2840 Computer and Network Security]]
- [[IY2760 Introduction to Information Security]]
- Understanding of operational technology (OT) versus IT (desirable)
- [[CS2850 Operating Systems]]
outcomes: Understand the architecture and components of industrial control systems (ICS, SCADA, PLCs)
Identify security vulnerabilities specific to cyber-physical systems
Apply security standards and frameworks for critical infrastructure
Conduct risk assessments for safety-critical systems

modules.title: Applications of Cryptography
modules.overview: This module covers the practical application of cryptographic techniques to secure systems. Topics include symmetric encryption algorithms (AES, ChaCha20), asymmetric encryption (RSA, ECC), hash functions, message authentication codes, digital signatures, key management and PKI, cryptographic protocols (TLS, SSH, PGP), post-quantum cryptography, and implementation considerations (side-channel resistance, constant-time implementation).
modules.prerequisitesText:
- [[IY2760 Introduction to Information Security]]
- [[CS1860 Mathematical Structures]] (number theory, modular arithmetic)
- Programming proficiency (C or Python recommended)

modules.title: User-Centred Design
modules.overview: This module introduces the principles and practices of user-centred design (UCD). Topics include user research methods (interviews, surveys, observation), persona development, user journey mapping, information architecture, interaction design, prototyping (low and high fidelity), usability evaluation methods, accessibility standards (WCAG), and iterative design processes. The module emphasises designing digital products that meet user needs and provide positive user experiences.

assessment: Coursework: User research reports and analysis
Practical assignments: Prototyping and design exercises
Project: End-to-end user-centred design process for a digital product
Portfolio: Design process documentation with rationale

modules.title: Data Analysis
modules.overview: This module covers the theory and practice of data analysis from a computational perspective. Topics include exploratory data analysis, statistical inference, hypothesis testing, regression analysis, Bayesian methods, time series analysis, causal inference, and reproducible research practices. The module emphasises rigorous statistical methodology applied to real-world datasets using modern data analysis tools.

- [[CS2900 Multi-dimensional Data Processing]]
- Programming proficiency (Python, R)

Practical assignments: Statistical modelling and inference exercises

modules.title: On-line Machine Learning
modules.overview: This module covers machine learning in settings where data arrives sequentially and models must be updated incrementally. Topics include online learning algorithms (FTRL, Hedge algorithm, exponentiated gradient), bandit problems (multi-armed bandits, contextual bandits), regret analysis, concept drift detection, active learning, and applications in recommendation systems, advertising, and real-time prediction.

modules.title: Large-Scale Data Storage and Processing
modules.overview: This module covers technologies and techniques for storing, processing, and analysing data at scale. Topics include distributed file systems (HDFS), NoSQL databases (key-value, document, column-family, graph), MapReduce and Spark programming models, stream processing, data warehousing, and distributed query processing. modules.title: Visualisation and Exploratory Analysis
modules.overview: This module covers the principles and practices of data visualisation and exploratory data analysis. modules.title: Business Intelligence Systems, Infrastructures and Technologies
modules.overview: This module covers the design, implementation, and management of business intelligence systems. modules.overview: This module explores advanced topics in distributed systems and computer networks. modules.title: Deep Learning

Topics include advanced neural network architectures (transformers, graph neural networks, normalising flows), self-supervised learning, meta-learning, neural architecture search, model compression and distillation, interpretability and explainability, and ethical considerations in deep learning. modules.overview: This module covers the design and implementation of autonomous systems that perceive, reason, and act in real-world environments. Topics include sensor integration, state estimation and localisation, mapping (SLAM), path planning, decision-making under uncertainty (POMDPs), robot control architectures, and autonomous vehicle systems. modules.overview: This module provides a comprehensive introduction to reinforcement learning.
